$comment: The dispatch-time routing registry. Shape decided by ADR-035; contents from ADR-032 section 3 as
that ADR amends it. Validated against harness/model-map.schema.json by
cli/internal/harness/model_map.go, which reads the schema as data rather than restating it.
NOT EMBEDDED, and that is deliberate. triggers.go next door carries a //go:embed copy and
falls back to it when the repo file is missing. For a routing map that is disqualifying: an
absent file would resolve to a build-time default and every check downstream would call it
healthy. Constraint C15 — a map that cannot be read fails loudly, never as empty and never as
a permissive default. See #1137 for the drift the embedded triggers copy already carries.
CONCURRENCY IS DECLARED, NOT ENFORCED. This is level 1 of ADR-035's split. Nothing decrements
these numbers today because a dispatcher would, and `dotf agent` is still an unknown command.
Level 2 will bound only what dotf itself launches, and the honest guarantee stays narrow:
'dotf alone will never be the cause of exhaustion', never 'exhaustion will not happen'.
As of #1150 PR-Agent runs on mimo-v2.5, so `pr-agent-ci` below still shares this
subscription but no longer contends for the deepseek bucket that `dotf spec review`
draws on. The sharing stays declared; the contention it caused does not.
NaN's limit is PER MODEL, not per API key — measured 2026-08-20: eight concurrent requests to
deepseek returned 5x200 and 3x429 while mimo answered 200 throughout that saturation. So a
second NaN model is a second lane, and a chain that falls through to one is not merely
retrying into the same wall. The reserve is static; adaptive reservation is out of scope.
THE `top` TIER HAS NO FALLBACK, on purpose (ADR-032 section 4). Degrading the top tier silently is
how a gate becomes a green checkmark. It queues or escalates; it does not quietly get cheaper.
`openrouter` and `codex` are both absent because they are RETIRED, not because they were
overlooked: openrouter was deleted upstream in August 2026, and codex is no longer used by
this operator (confirmed 2026-08-21). ADR-032 section 3 referenced a `codex` pool it never declared;
the resolution is deletion, not declaration. They are named here so the absences read as
decisions, which is why the assertions are structural rather than a grep for these words.
TIERS ARE KEYED BY WHATEVER CONSUMES THE MODEL ID, which is not always a harness.
`claude` and `opencode` render the id into their own agent definition, so they key by harness.
`nan` keys by POOL, because the harnesses that reach it (`pi`, `agy`) take the model as a launcher
flag rather than a rendered field — `pi --model X`, `agy --model X`. So `pi` correctly has no tier
entry: its render is `adapter`, and there is no rendered definition to put a model id into. Asking
for a tier keyed `pi` is a question about a field that does not exist, which is why ResolveTier
errors rather than inventing one. A harness whose render is `adapter` keys by its pool.
Model ids: alias where the harness self-rotates, canonical id where it does not. Claude Code
accepts opus/sonnet/haiku, which resolve to the current member of each family, so rotation
costs nothing there. Every other pool takes the canonical id.

nan.concurrency_note: per model, not per API key — measured 2026-08-20
nan.why: Reasoning-class models on a flat subscription. The pool CI and the TUI both draw from, which is why the reserve exists.

claude.why: The only harness with a session-time execution surface, so the only one where a hook can fire rather than an instruction being remembered.

copilot.why: Seat-based, so concurrency is a fleet property rather than a number this map can state honestly.

opencode.why: The daily driver TUI. Draws on the NaN catalog through its own provider config.

pi.why: pi is not a pool; it is the harness that reaches NaN, and the only one with no declarative agent format — hence render: adapter (#563).

agy.why: Present in the reviewer pool as the provider-diverse fallback arm, so it belongs in the map that routes to it.
